blogs.title: "Beyond Four Thousand Tokens" — Why Long Context Matters
blogs.description: An introductory look at why most LLMs cap at ~4K tokens, the everyday problems that arise in real‑world tasks like full‑book summarisation or multi‑document reasoning, and how extending context can unlock new kinds of AI experiences.

blogs.title: "What’s Inside Rotations" — A Gentle Guide to RoPE
blogs.description: A light‑hearted explanation of Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), how they encode order into every token’s hidden state, why feeding the model new positions hurts performance, and what previous tricks (linear scaling, NTK, YaRN) have tried to fix.

blogs.title: "Uneven Horizons" — Discovering Two Flavors of Non‑Uniformity
blogs.description: How the authors found that not all rotary angles behave alike—low-frequency dimensions need less tweaking than high-frequency ones—and that early tokens deserve special treatment too. These surprising observations set the stage for a smarter interpolation method.

blogs.title: "Evolution Meets Embeddings" — Searching For the Best Angle Rescales
blogs.description: A clear walk‑through of the evolutionary search algorithm used by LongRoPE, describing how it quickly hones in on per‑dimension rescale factors that preserve information better than earlier uniform methods while staying computationally cheap.

blogs.title: "Stepping Stones To Millions" — The Progressive Extension Strategy
blogs.description: "Instead of leaping straight into two million tokens", LongRoPE takes small pasture steps—fine‑tune at just 256k tokens, then re‑interpolate once more—to reach >2M contexts with only ~1K extra training steps.

blogs.title: "Proof Through Numbers" — Real‑World Gains From LongRoPE
blogs.description: Concrete evidence that longer windows pay off: lower perplexity all the way up past two million tokens, strong passkey‑retrieval scores from long passages, plus benchmark stability when running small queries—all showing every bit counts.
